Experimental prototype

Fedimint ecash on a card.

Fedimint Card puts the spend keys for Fedimint ecash on a contactless chip. You tap the card at a till and type its PIN, and the card signs the payment itself. It is an experimental prototype, tested with small amounts on one federation.

Get the POS app and Card 4.0 till

See it work

A till tops up the card by Lightning. The holder types the PIN, taps the card, and the card signs the payment.

How a payment works

The card does one job: it signs with keys that were made on its chip, after its PIN. The till, the card registry and the federation do everything else.

  1. Set up the card

    An operator's phone sets up a blank card in one tap. The chip makes its own spend keys, and the card gets a PIN of 4 to 8 digits.

  2. Load it at a till

    Review the card credit, fixed top-up fee and total on the POS. Pay the Lightning invoice and tap the card to load the agreed amount.

  3. Tap and type the PIN

    The till builds the payment, and the card signs it after the PIN is typed on the till's phone. The card signs for the notes used in the purchase.

  4. The federation settles

    The guardians check the signature and mark the notes spent. Change goes back to fresh keys on the card in the same transaction.

Cards / NXP J3R180

Where to get cards

The Fedimint Card applet runs on NXP J3R180 cards (JCOP 4, Java Card 3.0.5) with contact and contactless interfaces, the same cards Cashu Card uses. Choose blank cards compatible with the Setup app, then set them up with the Fedimint Card Setup app (Google Play, TestFlight) or install the applet from a computer.

Risks to know

Fedimint Card is an experimental prototype, and its applet and till code have had no outside security review. Keep only small amounts on a card, amounts you can afford to lose.

  • The federation holds the bitcoin.

    Fedimint ecash is a claim on one federation. If enough of its guardians fail or act together against you, the ecash loses its value.

  • A lost or wiped card loses its ecash.

    The spend keys are made on the card and never leave it, so ecash whose keys are gone cannot be recovered. Keep the card somewhere safe.

  • Pay only at tills you trust.

    Check the amount on the merchant’s phone before you authorize the purchase. The card checks the holder’s PIN when it signs.

  • The registry can see balances.

    Each card's notes are kept in the card registry at registry.fedimintcard.org, which sees every card's balance and payment history (see Privacy).

  • Some amounts cannot be paid.

    A card holds up to 32 notes (the first cards hold 8), and the change from a payment has to fit in its free ones. When it does not, the till refuses the payment.

  • Top-ups round to card amounts.

    A top-up is split into at most three notes, up to 100,000 sats, so the amount loaded can differ slightly from the amount asked for. The POS shows that amount and the fee before payment. Any unused fee stays with the merchant.

  • Offline payments settle later.

    A paired POS phone with its offline kit ready can take eligible payments while disconnected. It sends them to the till when it reconnects. Keep those payments on the phone until they settle.

  • The apps are public betas.

    Fedimint Card Setup is in early access on Google Play and in TestFlight on iPhone, and Fedimint Card POS is in early access on Google Play and in TestFlight. For a fresh Android installation, the signed Card 4.0 POS APK is also available. The Fedi app cannot load cards.
